One of the things that I would attribute that to, and I don't know if I've talked about this last year at a previous presentation, but is COVID and some of the booking restrictions that are placed on us because of COVID. People committing property crimes are not typically those who were accepted by the jail. So if we caught somebody, we had to just let them go. And people that commit property crimes, that's what they do when they're out. We are the Puget Sound Auto Theft Task Force. text: Go ahead, sir. Yeah. I keep reading on social media about the issue that the Tacoma News Tribune highlighted last weekend about the street racing and blocking off streets and doing donuts. They don't show up in the statistics, but how prevalent is that? And do you have a plan for controlling it?

speaker: mikezaro
text: We do. And thanks for bringing that up, Alan, because that's pretty timely. So we haven't seen a ton of it here in Lakewood, not like Tacoma and Fife have. And certainly the South King County agencies have been dealing with it for years. But the title street racing is a little misleading because they don't do a lot of racing. They just drive around really fast and then they'll in mass block an intersection and allow cars in to do donuts in the middle of the intersection. And these are live intersections where traffic's supposed to be going through. So we've seen it a couple times. This last weekend, it was actually a regional emphasis on the part of all law enforcement agencies because we knew an event, and I'll call it, that was going to be held starting in Tacoma, where a large group of these folks were gonna come down and try and do this. And what we were able to do is kind of meet them wherever they went and dissuade them from engaging in that activity. And eventually, after about two hours of trying, they gave up. And it really does. And I came out Saturday night to watch this. And what I walked away with was, it's not hard to manage necessarily, but it is resource intensive because it really does take a regional effort just by virtue of how mobile they are. They were on Saturday night, they were in Tacoma, they were in Fife, they were in Puyallup and Lakewood, unincorporated Pierce County. I think they went up to Edgewood once. So you really have to have a regional effort. And all of the jurisdictions in Pierce County are zeroed in on this and they're all participating. So it hopefully will kind of fizzle out and not grow beyond what it is now and maybe even go away. But that's what the story was about. And again, don't be misled by the term racing. It's not actually racing and it's not cruising like you remember back when you were kids, but it is dangerous, dangerous activity that puts a lot of people at risk and is very disruptive for people trying to drive through traffic.

speaker: alanhart
